summary: Grant CI runner access to release-engineering group and support secret rotation for release pipelines
description:
Issue summary:
The Release Engineering team cannot run scheduled release pipelines that require access to the shared GitLab runners and ephemeral credentials in Vault. We need a scoped permission change and a documented, supported process for automated secret rotation in the release pipelines.

Impact:
- Blocked nightly release smoke runs for stable branch (delays release validation).
- Manual intervention required to restart pipelines when runner jobs fail with credential errors.
- Risk of stale credentials in production deployment workflows.

Context / Background:
- Release pipelines execute on shared GitLab runners tagged 'release' and assume ephemeral credentials stored in Vault (production path: secret/data/releases/prod).
- Earlier this week we tightened runner token policy; some runner tokens were rotated and a subset of runner registrations lost the 'run-as-group: release-engineering' TTL.

Requested outcome:
1) Restore runner permissions for the release-engineering group so scheduled pipelines run without manual restart.
2) Implement or document a supported secret-rotation hook in the release pipeline that safely re-reads rotated Vault credentials without human steps.
3) Provide rollback steps and an owner to contact if rotation causes failures.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger nightly release pipeline (Project: infra/releases, pipeline: nightly-smoke).
2) Observe jobs that request secret 'secret/data/releases/prod' fail with 403 or credential-not-found errors inside the vault-agent step.
3) Check runner status in GitLab admin (Admin Area -> Runners) and filter tag 'release' to see 'not connected' vs 'online' and check 'run-as' metadata for group TTLs.
expected_behavior: Nightly release pipelines should run on 'release' runners and retrieve ephemeral credentials from Vault transparently, with no manual secrets refresh required.
actual_behavior: Jobs fail with credential errors and/or are queued indefinitely because runners show limited permissions or are failing the vault-agent step after a backend token rotation.
logs_and_links: Vault audit tail sample: /var/log/vault/audit.log (attached to ticket in case files)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Marcus Lee: Opening ticket after on-call confirmed reproducible failures for nightly smoke runs. Attaching sample job logs and Vault audit tail. Requesting runbook update and temporary fix to avoid blocking today's release window.

2026-03-10 11:02 - Sofia Martinez: Oncall will investigate runner metadata and Vault token TTLs. Initial hypothesis: runner registration tokens expired during the policy roll that ran last saturday. Will validate runner configs and the CI service account's ACL for the 'releases' path in Vault.

2026-03-10 14:28 - DevOps SRE (Ivan Korhonen): Found three release-tagged runners with missing 'run_as_group' capability due to token mismatch. Re-registered two runners as immediate mitigation; re-registration required elevated token. Pipeline now progressed past vault-agent but one job still failed with 403. Investigating vault policies for the CI service account.

2026-03-11 08:07 - Release Eng (Priya Nair): We attempted a scheduled rotation of 'releases/prod' credentials yesterday which may have invoked a replace-with-new-secret mode. We need an idempotent read-in-place step in the pipelines so rotated secrets are picked up without manual restart. Priya can pair with ops to run a test rotation in staging.

2026-03-12 10:46 - Sofia Martinez: Implemented short-term fix: bumped runner registration TTL and reissued runner tokens for the release group; updated ACL to allow 'ci-service@redwood' read on secret/data/releases/prod. Next steps: add a Vault-renew/refresh step to the pipeline and create CI token rotation playbook. Scheduling follow-up task INT-6190 to document automation and runbook.
investigation_notes: Checked GitLab admin logs: token rotation event on 2026-03-07 at 03:20 UTC correlated with runners losing registration metadata.
Vault audit entries show client 'ci-service' attempted to read secret and received 403 starting 2026-03-10 01:06 UTC until ACL change applied.
Hypothesis: Runner re-registration happened but Vault policy for 'ci-service' was not updated to include the new accessor ID for the rotated credential, causing 403s until manual ACL patch.
Tested re-registering runners in staging and confirmed that pipeline job successfully reads rotated secret when 'vault-agent' sidecar is restarted within the job container.

Risk assessment: If we automate rotation without pipeline refresh semantics, running jobs may continue to hold old credentials leading to intermittent failures across releases. Need an atomic handshake or short TTL for secrets with automated refresh logic.
resolution_notes: Short-term: Re-registered two release runners and updated ci-service ACLs in Vault so nightly pipelines proceeded. Added a Vault read/renew helper step to the pipeline (branch: release-fixes/runner-refresh) as a temporary mitigation. Long-term actions scheduled: INT-6190 to add a robust secret-rotation orchestration (pipeline hook + operator runbook) and INT-6191 to add monitoring and alerting when runner metadata or vault reads fail. Owner for follow-ups: Priya Nair (Release Engineering).
